description: Mobility is an open-source Python package for simulating daily personal and work travel in a local territory. Its maintainers describe a workflow that builds a synthetic population, multimodal networks and activity opportunities, then estimates travel diaries and origin-destination flows. Users provide a study area's zones, socioeconomic and transport data, network costs and a scenario. Outputs include mode shares, travel times, distances, emissions and diagnostic comparisons. Geographic coverage is mainly France and Switzerland in the documented workflows, from individual zones to regions of several hundred communes. MIT source, package instructions and examples are public. A limitation is that default parameters are only a starting point; local surveys and calibration are needed before route or project decisions. Mobility can test new public-transit lines, cycling access and land-use changes. The catalogue's model-sumo is a distinct microscopic traffic simulator, not this activity-demand model. No survey, network or package was downloaded.
inputs: Local population, activities and multimodal networks
name: Mobility local travel demand simulator
notes: G7 G7-1464. Prepared draft only. Metadata review on 2026-09-28; no models, data or archives downloaded. Related-resource comparisons are reviewer mappings, not tested interoperability.
outputs: Daily travel diaries and origin-destination flows
